main_text.p: pora cum aeris temperie, vel intemperie dili- genter perpendere expedit, vt quifque pro pe- culiari & vernacula natura aere competente & conueniente fruatur, noxiumq; euitet.

Primum mundi regiones feu cardines I V. vt Oriens calidus & ficcus, Occidens frigidus & humidus, Septentrio frigidus & ficcus, Meridies calidus & humidus : quibus cardinibus venti temperamento & natura correspondent, quod hi naturam fc.loci, per quem spirant, in- duant & affumant, auster videlic. calidus & humidus omnium infalubertrimus, pernitiofus n, femper, morborum namq; feminaria maligna ex meridionalibus illis locis & regionibus, vt Italia, Gallia, & bona parte Hispaniæ fecum exportare, ac in Germaniam nostrā deponere fat testaturexperientia, quāuis & apud nos ra- dices & feminaria malignorum morborū im- mutabilia, quaq; interdum sua sede & loco ex- cludinō possint, sponte generari nō negārim.
Zephyrus frigidus est & humidus. Boreas, iudicio Plinii, & testimonio populorum Septentrionis faluberrimus, vt & Eurus qui ab Oriente flat.

Itaq; faluberrimi sunt dies sereni, meliores pluuiofi quam nebulofi, optimiq; hieme qui omnino vento carent, statim quibus Fauonius perflat. Occidentalem enim ventum, non plā- ne infalubrem esse & noxium testantur popu- li Occidentis : imò Euro sepe salubriorem eum.

page.notes: Left-margin catchwords and the very small heading marks ("Aufter", "cur ven-", "torum in-", "faluber-", "rimum?") at the left edge are marginal running signposts, not body text; they are transcribed in the notes as printed. Several words in the lower half are hard to read at this scan resolution and are uncertain; the text of the last paragraph and the Greek-free Latin of the middle columns should be checked against the original. The printed sentence "quā sede ... sponte" and words such as "cludinō possint" and "Zephyrus frigidus est" are read from a degraded image and may contain errors. Some left-edge words are cut off by the binding.
